listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, November 23. Our lead story is the climate summit. The COP31 talks have ended with no deal. They were the longest-running climate talks in United Nations history. Negotiations broke down two days after they were due to end. The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted, blamed difficult geopolitical times. Reports say about two hundred countries met in Antalya, Turkey, and could not agree on fossil fuels. Fossil fuels are the primary driver of global warming. Now to the front page. In tech, Anthropic announced the closing of its initial public offering. That includes full exercise of the underwriters' option to buy additional shares, and a concurrent private placement. In sports, the San Francisco 49ers beat the Vikings thirty-five to ten in Mexico City. The win moves them to nine and one and keeps them in the top seed in the NFC. In world news, NATO meets today over last week's missile strikes in Poland. The Russia-Ukraine war has again reached European territory, with ship attacks and allegations about a Russian plot in Denmark. In politics, Democrats have won at least two hundred fifty-eight House seats in the midterms. Republicans hold at least one hundred seventy-three. It is the largest Democratic majority since nineteen ninety-two. Now the sections. In tech, Simon Willison had Claude build a page showing every way to style an HTML select box. A popular agent skills framework is also trending on GitHub. In politics, The Lever reports that Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has pushed Trump into talks on Medicare for All. NPR says Republicans are debating their future after the midterm losses. In world news, Kenya and Congo agreed to restore ties. Zelensky says Ukrainian drones hit Russian ships off Libya. In sports, Navajo Stirling knocked out Jiri Prochazka at UFC Qatar to stay unbeaten at twelve and zero. The Braves tendered contracts to four players. In Atlanta, street repaving has started across Buckhead. A major housing development has broken ground near Topgolf and The Works. Delta says its automated flight systems are working again after Sunday's delays. In architecture, we have the Bahá'í Temple of South America in Santiago. We also have the Yokohama Timber Wharf in Japan. In science, new research explains how Challenger Deep became the deepest spot in the ocean. NASA has put a new laser instrument in Svalbard. And bumblebees turn out to be problem solvers. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
lead.note: The COP31 climate summit has ended without a deal. It was the longest-running climate talks in United Nations history, and negotiations broke down two days after they were due to finish. The summit was held in Antalya, and the prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted, attributed the failure to what he called difficult geopolitical times. Other coverage says roughly 200 countries took part and that they could not agree on fossil fuels, which are the primary driver of global warming. The result leaves open the question of what comes next for the annual process, and BBC coverage is already asking that. For a reader who follows science, oceans and the built environment, the outcome matters because climate commitments shape energy, building and development policy for years ahead. The talks were meant to produce an agreement. They did not, and the divisions between countries are now plain to see.
